# Customer registration review fixture
This is a source-and-schema review fixture, not a standalone Spring build.
Target: Java 17, Spring Data JPA 4.1.1, Jakarta Persistence 3.2, PostgreSQL 17.
The existing PostgreSQL JDBC driver exposes PSQLException; retain the project's installed driver.

Two independent application replicas use this database, with no inter-process lock.
The supplied schema is the effective schema for a disposable empty test database.
Requests enter register() without an ambient transaction. The supplied transaction configuration is used by both replicas; repositories and the transaction manager share the same EntityManagerFactory.
emailKey is validated upstream as non-null lowercase ASCII; exact equality of that normalized key is the accepted uniqueness rule.
The requirement is at most one committed customer per emailKey. An existing key returns DUPLICATE; other storage failures remain failures.
UUID primary keys are generated independently per attempt. The ORM uses the nullable version property to detect new Customer instances.

The source excerpts omit framework wiring/build files. Do not treat their presence as proof of deployed database behavior.
Review the proposed Java-local locking suggestion against the actual persistence contract. A complete database test needs the normal project dependencies and an isolated PostgreSQL 17 database.
files.review-note.md:
The sequential acceptance scenario is: register the same normalized emailKey twice, receiving CREATED then DUPLICATE.
One reviewer proposes adding synchronized to Registration.register because it contains an existence query followed by save.
Before changing the method, review the schema, transaction setup and exception boundary. Preserve the accepted at-most-one-committed-row requirement across both replicas.

prerequisites: Source review requires no running service.
For an integration run, use only a disposable empty PostgreSQL17 database and the existing Java17/SpringDataJPA4.1.1 project toolchain. No installation or upgrade is implied.

Determine which findings the supplied evidence supports, preserve adequate safeguards, and give the smallest justified changes plus a reproducible validation plan. You may edit supplied source/schema fixtures for review; do not provision services or apply production migrations. Separate source-level conclusions from unexecuted integration claims.

evaluatorOnlyCriteria.decisiveConstraint: Only CREATE INDEX versus CREATE UNIQUE INDEX differs in db/schema.sql. The index name itself is identical and does not establish uniqueness.
sharedExpected: Inspect deployed-schema fixture, callers, two-replica scope, READ_COMMITTED transaction and catch outside TransactionTemplate.execute.
Distinguish a precheck interleaving from violation of the persisted invariant under the effective constraint.
Preserve normalized non-null key scope, exact duplicate-email exception classification, and rollback/commit boundary.
Do not rely on synchronized to coordinate independent application replicas.
Keep Java/framework baseline and avoid provisioning/installing services or claiming unexecuted checks.

expected: Identify that the named uq_customer_email_key is a nonunique index; no effective cross-replica protection is provided by the existence check or READ_COMMITTED alone.
Recommend a database unique safeguard for the accepted normalized key, with appropriate existing-data/migration considerations if promoted beyond the empty fixture.
Retain the precheck as advisory if desired and keep error translation around the complete owning transaction.
Propose a two-connection concurrent test that pauses both after absence checks and verifies one committed row, correct loser result and no failed-transaction continuation.
failures: Infers uniqueness from the uq_ name.
Treats @Transactional/TransactionTemplate or synchronized as sufficient cross-replica uniqueness.
Suppresses arbitrary integrity/storage errors as duplicates.
Declares a database integration test passed without running it.

expected: Recognize the existing unique index enforces the key invariant despite a possible stale precheck.
Do not report duplicate committed rows as a confirmed defect under the supplied schema; reject the synchronized change as unnecessary for that invariant.
Preserve existing targeted translation around a transaction whose commit occurs before execute returns.
Request or propose a real concurrent integration test to confirm adapter translation and outcome handling; source guarantees do not establish observed production frequency.
failures: Reports the same missing-uniqueness defect as case A without inspecting UNIQUE.
Adds a redundant second index, global lock or framework redesign to satisfy an already-protected invariant.
Removes exact exception translation or broadens it to all integrity violations.
Claims the unique index serializes all business logic or makes every repository operation atomic.

Commit the winner and resolve the other transaction; inspect row count and concrete SQLSTATE/constraint identity.

reproduction.expectedObservations: Case A can commit two rows; case B permits at most one same-key row and rejects the conflicting insert. These are source-grounded expectations, not executed results.
